issues.strongest_rebuttal: The unconditional HighwayMode-to-enter_hwy edge exists, and the guarded FinishState edges are compiler-owned route-control members. They may not alter ordinary startup, but the deterministic initial-entry facts identify them as conditional initial transitions and the source contract does not authorize such alternatives.
issues.title: Conditional HighwayMode Initial Completion Entries

issues.basis: NL6 source transition tr_000? is represented by the authored HighwayMode-to-FinishState relation in PlantUML/canonical source, while the closed inspection inventory shows HighwayMode transitions only to UrbanMode or [*]; FinishState is reached through child initial/route-control segments rather than a resolved direct HighwayMode endpoint.
issues.expected: A resolved transition has source HighwayMode and target FinishState.
issues.observed: No closed transition has resolved_source_ref state:HighwayMode:line:17 and resolved_target_ref state:FinishState:line:21; the relevant outer termination transition is transition:line:75 from HighwayMode to [*].
issues.reason: The source requires a direct HighwayMode-to-FinishState transition. The closed model has HighwayMode-to-final-pseudostate and internal route-control edges, but no resolved transition whose target is FinishState from HighwayMode. The exact source and target state refs are therefore the negative-edge evidence.
issues.requirement_quote: A transition from HighwayMode to FinishState must exist.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model contains compiler-generated internal [*] -> FinishState edges and a HighwayMode -> [*] route-control edge, which may implement the authored composite exit through macro expansion. The supplied working contract requires whole-macro closure; the visible inventory does not provide a resolved direct HighwayMode-to-FinishState endpoint, so the contrast remains candidate evidence.
issues.title: Missing Direct Highway Completion Edge

issues.basis: NL6 establishes termination semantics; inspection-equivalent facts show HighwayMode outgoing transitions to UrbanMode and [*], with transition:line:75 targeting [*], and conditional initial transitions lines 22-24 targeting FinishState. Reference inspection also records a self-via-parent route-control transition at AutonomousMode line 90, reinforcing nonterminal composite routing.
issues.expected: HighwayMode stably completes by reaching FinishState without re-entering continued behavior.
issues.observed: HighwayMode has transition:line:75 to [*] under R45RouteToken == 29, while FinishState is reached through separate conditional initial/route-control structure; the surrounding AutonomousMode also has a self transition at transition:line:90 under R45RouteToken == 29.
issues.reason: The designated FinishState is present and reachable, but the exact HighwayMode termination structure includes a HighwayMode-to-final-pseudostate route and conditional internal initial routes to FinishState, so the composite's termination behavior is not represented as a stable direct completion relation. This is distinct from endpoint existence.
issues.requirement_quote: HighwayMode must terminate by reaching FinishState.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The route-control expansion may be intended to implement completion through macro sequencing, and FinishState itself is present and reachable. The supplied closure does not establish a stable terminal execution certificate for the composite, so the stronger termination property remains a precise unsupported-boundary candidate.
issues.title: HighwayMode Termination Routes Through Nonterminal Structure

issues.basis: NL12 establishes CollisionAvoidance as an initially operating system with required active/deactive behavior; inspection-equivalent and verify facts report CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active unreachable from initial entry. The owner-local edge transition:line:86 exists but does not establish root reachability.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance system is entered from the model's top-level initial configuration in collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidance and both descendants are unreachable from top-level initial entry, although transition:line:86 locally enters collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.reason: The exact CollisionAvoidance owner-local initial edge to collision_avoidance_deactive exists, but the entire CollisionAvoidance composite is unreachable from any top-level initial entry. Consequently the required initial operating scope and its response states cannot execute from the model root.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL states the system's initial state but does not explicitly require CollisionAvoidance to be connected to the same top-level root as AutonomousMode; the local owner entry is exact and present. The root-level reachability defect is therefore kept separate in the derived contract.
issues.title: Collision Avoidance Initial Scope Is Unreachable

issues.basis: NL12 source semantics and exact source inventory identify CollisionAvoidance as an operating composite; closed inspection reachability excludes state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 and its descendants; verify check reachability:state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 is refuted.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance is reachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.observed: state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 is not reachable from top-level initial entry; its local initial edge transition:line:86 is also unreachable.
issues.reason: The source-defined CollisionAvoidance composite owns the required collision-avoidance behavior, but the complete closed hierarchy cannot reach that composite from top-level initial entry. This causal gap is a distinct root reachability obligation and is not discharged by the local CollisionAvoidance initial edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source presents CollisionAvoidance as a separate top-level composite, and separate top-level composites may be independently instantiated or evaluated. The supplied finite hierarchy nevertheless defines root reachability and explicitly refutes it for CollisionAvoidance.
issues.title: Collision Avoidance Scope Unreachable From Root

issues.basis: NL12; transition:line:87; state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83; inspection diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify reachability refutation for CollisionAvoidance.
issues.expected: The activation transition must support the stated pedestrian, rear-distance/velocity, and mode-specific front-distance stimuli.
issues.observed: The transition at transition:line:87 has the combined closed-model trigger and is declared, but its consumer state is unreachable from the top-level initial entry, so the required response is not operationally reachable.
issues.reason: The required activation transition exists and is declared, but its owning CollisionAvoidance composite is not reachable from any top-level initial entry; the deterministic consumer fact reports no reachable consumer transition.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode).

issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance must be reachable from a top-level initial entry so its required activation behavior can occur.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidance and both of its descendants are marked unreachable from the top-level initial entry; the finite reachability check is refuted for CollisionAvoidance.
issues.reason: The source-declared CollisionAvoidance operating scope is absent from the finite root-reachable set. Its internal initial edge exists, but no top-level initial entry reaches the composite, so the required activation behavior cannot be exercised from the system start.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode).
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The collision-avoidance composite has a valid internal initial edge and both required internal transitions, but no supplied top-level reachability edge enters the composite.
issues.title: Collision avoidance scope is unreachable

issues.observed: transition:line:88 has the exact endpoints and trigger, but its consumer state is unreachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact deactivation transition exists with the required closed-model trigger, but its active-state consumer is outside the root-reachable set, so the required return behavior cannot be reached operationally.

issues.title: Collision deactivation consumer is unreachable

issues.basis: NL6; exact FinishState target; closed transitions transition:line:36 and transition:line:40 from FinishState to the enclosing final state; finite model also contains continued parent routing.
issues.expected: Once HighwayMode reaches FinishState, the HighwayMode operation must stably terminate at FinishState.
issues.observed: FinishState is reachable but has outgoing transitions on urban_way=true and auto_finished=true, allowing continued routing out of the HighwayMode composite.
issues.reason: The required HighwayMode-to-FinishState transition exists, but FinishState remains a child of HighwayMode and has outgoing parent-exit transitions. Reaching FinishState therefore does not establish stable termination of the HighwayMode scope.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The named FinishState exists and the completion endpoint is present; the contrary evidence is the target's active-ancestor continuation, so endpoint existence alone does not settle stable termination.
issues.title: Highway termination is not stable

issues.basis: NL10; exact FinishState binding; transition:line:21 from straight to final routing and transition:line:23 from intersection to final routing; parent-level continued exits and mode routing are present in the closed inventory.
issues.expected: Once UrbanMode completes, reaching FinishState must stably terminate the UrbanMode operation.
issues.observed: UrbanMode has reachable continuation paths and its completion routing targets a FinishState owned by HighwayMode; the target has outgoing transitions, so stable termination is not established.
issues.reason: The required completion endpoint exists, but the target FinishState is nested in HighwayMode and has outgoing transitions. The closed model also contains continued routing from UrbanMode and its descendants, so reaching the named target does not establish stable UrbanMode termination.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The completion transitions are present and FinishState is declared; the unresolved semantic gap is stable termination because the exact target and active ancestors retain continuations.
issues.title: Urban termination is not stable
